newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel rallies higher late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel rallies higher late.

text.p: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel fuel prices jumped sharply by late Wednesday as the strength in differentials outpaced the modest drop in NYMEX prices.
The surge in low sulphur diesel prices started Tuesday in the U.S. Gulf (USG) as players holding barrels moved to the sidelines, forcing traders with short positions to chase prices up.
The USG strength in turn boosted New York Harbor (NYH) differentials, according to traders.
"I'm not surprised about the Gulf or the (midcontinent), but the strength in the Harbor was a bit of a shock," one player said.
"I don't think there's any fewer barrels today than there were yesterday," the trader added.

Market watchers said Mobil's shutdown of the 65,000 barrel per day hydrotreater at its Joliet, Illinois refinery over the weekend following a small fire there sparked the jump. Reports that Mobil was selling crude oil in the spot market Tuesday led to concerns the unit would not return to operation soon.
USG front seventh cycle low sulphur diesel was talked between 2.25 and 2.50 cents late in the day, slipping slightly from its peak but up about 1.0 cent from late Tuesday levels.
NYH prompt low sulphur barrels changed hands as high as 2.50 cents over the screen, up more than 1.00 cent on the day.

Both USG and NYH spot gasoline markets were thinly traded on Wednesday, with little impact seen from the American Petroleum Institute's weekly report showing a draw in overall gasoline stocks of 3.2 million barrels.
The API put distillate inventories down 1.6 million barrels and refinery operations up 0.5 percentage point.
